key_insight: DOPD shows that better distillation comes not from simply giving teacher or student more privileged input, but from using privileged information in a dual on-policy setup that avoids "privilege illusion." It improves capacity transfer by supervising student-generated trajectories with richer, more reliable token-level signals.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key failure mode in on-policy distillation: when privileged information is injected into the teacher or student, the resulting supervision can look strong but fail to reflect the student’s true transferable capability gap. This can mislead training and limit distillation performance.
method: Use dual on-policy distillation to pair student-sampled trajectories with token-level supervision.
Introduce privileged information carefully to improve supervision quality without conflating it with the student’s actual learning gap.
Design the training objective to preserve the benefits of on-policy distillation while reducing the risk of privilege illusion.
impact: For practitioners, DOPD offers a more reliable way to transfer teacher capabilities into smaller or cheaper student models. It can improve distillation quality and robustness, especially when standard on-policy distillation is limited by weak or misleading supervision sources.
